finding.claim: purge() calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can invoke purgeAll() (destructive purge operation).
finding.source: Any authenticated low-privilege user's HTTP request to the purge route (userFrom(r) at handlers.go:25 returns the caller; the caller's Perms lack "admin")

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) – caller identity from request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") return value ignored; no if/return/403

finding.guards_checked: Compared with rotateKeys (handlers.go:33-35), which correctly uses mustPerm and returns on false. purge uses the non-enforcing checkPerm and ignores its result. No other middleware or auth wrapper exists in the directory (only handlers.go); routing/middleware not visible, and any middleware would have to enforce admin itself. Assumes the route is reachable by non-admin authenticated users, which the missing check permits.

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12 returns a bool only, doesn't abort; result discarded at line 26; no middleware in directory)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin") as a bare statement, and checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) only returns a bool and never writes a 403 or aborts, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any caller who reaches the handler, unlike rotateKeys, which tests mustPerm at handlers.go:33.
